notes: Both *and*s joining *old* to *well stricken in years* are added: the Hebrew juxtaposes zāqēn and bāʾ with no conjunction morpheme (rule 14's closing sentences).

*well* is the ASV's intensifier inside bāʾ's own rendering *well stricken*; *yet* in the last clause answers to no morpheme and stays added, while the presentative *there* remains with nišʾărāh under rule 17.
The object suffix of lərištāh is promoted to subject of the English passive and written by no separate word.
